---
title: "toOrdinal()"
subtitle: "Convert cardinal numbers to ordinal numbers or words"
toc: true
---

## Usage

``` R
toOrdinal(cardinal_number, language = "English", convert_to = "ordinal_number")
```

## Arguments

`cardinal_number`{#cardinal_number}

:   A numeric vector of non-negative whole numbers. Missing values return `NA`.

`language`{#language}

:   A single string naming the language whose rules are used. Defaults to `"English"`.

`convert_to`{#convert_to}

:   Either `"ordinal_number"` (the default: the number followed by its ordinal indicator) or `"ordinal_word"`. Underscores and spaces are interchangeable and case is ignored.

## Value

A character vector the same length as `cardinal_number`.

## Description

Converts cardinal numbers to ordinal numbers by appending a language-specific ordinal indicator (see <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordinal_indicator>), or, where implemented, to ordinal words.

## Supported languages

`"Dutch"`, `"English"`, `"French"`, `"German"`, `"German_alt"`, `"Spanish"`, `"Swedish"` and `"Turkish"`. Matching is case-insensitive. `"German_alt"` uses the period convention (`1.`), as does Turkish for ordinal numbers.

  ---------- ------ ----- ------ ------
  Language   `1`    `2`   `3`    `11`
  English    1st    2nd   3rd    11th
  Dutch      1ste   2de   3de    11de
  French     1re    2e    3e     11e
  German     1te    2te   3te    11te
  Spanish    1.er   2.º   3.er   11.º
  Swedish    1:a    2:a   3:e    11:e
  Turkish    1\.    2\.   3\.    11\.
  ---------- ------ ----- ------ ------

## Ordinal words

`convert_to = "ordinal_word"` is implemented for Turkish, for numbers 0 to 999. Other languages signal an error rather than returning a guess.

## Examples

``` R
toOrdinal(1)
toOrdinal(1, language = "French")

toOrdinal(1:20)
toOrdinal(1:25, language = "French")

toOrdinal(c(11, 21, 100, 111))
toOrdinal(4, language = "Turkish", convert_to = "ordinal_word")
```
